subject: Polity
description: High Court: jurisdiction, appointment, writs, powers

questions.stem: How many HIGH COURTS are there in India?
questions.explanation: INDIA has 25 HIGH COURTS (as of 2024). NOT necessarily 1 per state — some HCs cover MULTIPLE states / UTs (e.g., GAUHATI HC covers Assam + Nagaland + Mizoram + Arunachal Pradesh; PUNJAB+HARYANA HC; BOMBAY HC covers Maharashtra + Goa + Dadra-NH + DD; MADRAS HC covers TN + Puducherry; KOLKATA HC covers WB + A&N). RECENT additions: TELANGANA HC (2019, separated from AP HC); AMARAVATI/ANDHRA HC (2019); LADAKH became Bench of J&K HC (2019). OLDEST: CALCUTTA HC (1862, with Bombay + Madras). Each HC has a CHIEF JUSTICE + several judges. Establishd by IHC ACT 1861. JURISDICTION: each HC has fixed territorial jurisdiction (state(s) it serves) + ORIGINAL + APPELLATE + WRIT jurisdiction.

questions.stem: HIGH COURT judges are APPOINTED by:
questions.explanation: Article 217 — HC judges appointed by PRESIDENT after consulting: (a) CHIEF JUSTICE OF INDIA, (b) GOVERNOR of the state, (c) CHIEF JUSTICE of that High Court (for non-CJ appointments). COLLEGIUM SYSTEM (since 1990s, evolved through SC judgements) — practical primacy for SC + HC Collegium (CJI + senior judges). Govt's ROLE limited; can return recommendations once. Recent: Govt's NJAC ACT 2014 was struck down by SC (2015) — preserved Collegium. QUALIFICATIONS for HC judge (Art 217): Indian citizen + (10 yrs as HC advocate OR 10 yrs as judicial officer). RETIREMENT age: 62. SC judges: 65 (since 1963). Salary + perks CHARGED on consolidated fund of state (Art 202 etc.).

questions.stem: HIGH COURT can issue WRITS under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 226 — HC can issue writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto) for: (a) ENFORCEMENT OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, AND (b) FOR ANY OTHER PURPOSE (= LEGAL rights too — much broader than SC's Article 32 which is FR-only). HC's writ jurisdiction is THUS WIDER than SC's. APPLICANT can choose: file writ in SC (if FR violation) OR HC (FR + other rights). Most writs go to HCs first (faster, cheaper). Article 32 (FR enforcement) — described by Ambedkar as 'HEART AND SOUL of Constitution'. Article 226 — important for: PIL (Public Interest Litigation), Govt accountability, civil-rights advocacy. INDIAN HCS handle ~40-50 lakh pending cases (massive backlog).

questions.stem: OLDEST HIGH COURT in India is at:
questions.explanation: Calcutta, Bombay, Madras HCs were ALL established 1862 (Indian High Courts Act 1861). Calcutta HC (Calcutta) is technically the OLDEST since established FIRST chronologically — 2 July 1862 (Bombay 14 Aug 1862; Madras 15 Aug 1862). ALLAHABAD HC came in 1866 — 4th oldest. INSIGHT: these HCs replaced earlier 'Supreme Courts' (Calcutta SC of 1774, Bombay SC of 1823, Madras SC of 1801) under British East India Company. CALCUTTA HC has historic importance — long oldest civil law in Asia. Famous original CASES involved British-Indian + private property. Building styles reflect colonial Indo-Saracenic + Gothic architecture. HC of Punjab + Haryana (Chandigarh) — common to two states + Chandigarh UT.

questions.stem: RETIREMENT age of High Court judge is:
questions.explanation: HC judges RETIRE at 62 (originally 60; raised to 62 by 15th Amendment 1963). SC judges retire at 65 (Article 124(2)). Other key retirement ages: CAG = 65 or 6 yrs (whichever first); Election Commission = 65 or 6 yrs; UPSC chair = 65 or 6 yrs; State PSC chair = 62 or 6 yrs; CIC chair = 65 or 5 yrs. PROPOSALS to raise HC retirement age to 65 (uniform with SC) — pending. POST-RETIREMENT BANS: HC judge cannot practise as advocate before any court (except SC); SC judge cannot practise before ANY court. Concerns about 'POST-RETIREMENT JOBS' (governor, panel chair, etc.) — independence questions. INSIGHT — judicial independence preserved by tenure security + salary protection; retirement caps avoid stagnation.

questions.stem: HIGH COURT judges can be REMOVED by:

options.option_text: Same procedure as SC judges (Pres after Parliament impeachment)
Governor of the state directly too alone (option here)
CJI's direct orders alone (option here) too alone
Ruling by High Court itself (option here) too alone

questions.explanation: HC judge REMOVAL = same as SC: by PRESIDENT, after Parliament passes IMPEACHMENT motion with SPECIAL MAJORITY (Art 217 read with Art 124(4)). Grounds: PROVED MISBEHAVIOUR or INCAPACITY. Rare in practice — never an HC judge has been impeached + actually removed. CASES considered: V. Ramaswamy (SC 1993, motion failed); Soumitra Sen (Calcutta HC 2011, RS passed but he RESIGNED before LS); Justice Dipak Mishra (motion attempted, dismissed). PROCEDURE: motion of 50+ MPs (LS) or 100+ (RS); 3-member committee investigates; if guilt found, both Houses must pass with 2/3 of members + simple majority of total. Designed to protect judicial INDEPENDENCE — political removal hard. Salary + service conditions also constitutionally PROTECTED.

questions.stem: Which HIGH COURT has the LARGEST number of judges (sanctioned strength)?
questions.explanation: ALLAHABAD HC (UP) — largest HC by sanctioned strength (~160 judges) + caseload (~10 lakh pending). Reflects UP's vast population (~24 crore). Located at Allahabad/Prayagraj; bench at Lucknow. Other large HCs: BOMBAY (~94 sanctioned), MADRAS (~75), PUNJAB+HARYANA (~85), CALCUTTA (~72), KARNATAKA (~62), DELHI (~60). SMALLEST: Sikkim HC (3 judges), Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya (each ~5 judges). SUPREME COURT (Article 124) — sanctioned 34 (CJI + 33 puisne); current strength near full. CASE BACKLOG critical issue: ~40-50 lakh in HCs, ~80,000 in SC. Modi govt's e-Courts mission, virtual hearings (post-COVID) aim to speed up justice — significant gains in disposal rates.
